summary: Stone observation tower on Cheaha Mountain in Cheaha State Park, Alabama, built by the CCC in 1934 and administered by ADCNR; NHLR-registered 2009. Public, climbable, with an entrance fee.

facts.design: Rubble stone observation tower; about 10-foot cab on a 40-foot native stone shaft (Register); walls two feet thick (marker)

staffing.status: occasionally used by Talladega National Forest to watch for smoke (marker)

access.note: Inside Cheaha State Park, which charges an entrance fee (marker). Visitors can climb the stairway inside to the observation deck (Encyclopedia of Alabama).

visit.trail_note: On the summit of Cheaha Mountain; the marker says it can be reached from Alabama Route 281. Check the park for current hours and closures.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register lists 1934 as build year but its text says 1934-35; Wikipedia says construction started 1933 and completed 1934; the marker says dedicated April 4, 1936. Story gives 1934 completion and 1936 dedication.

Register says the CCC built it atop the park lodge; Wikipedia says park offices and a gift shop originally occupied wings on either side of the tower. The story reports both and does not endorse the lodge claim.
Register lists ADCNR as administrator; the marker credits the USDA Forest Service and Alabama State Parks with erecting the marker. The story uses the Register's administrator.

notes_for_editor: Four independent sources agree on location, the 1934 completion and the CCC build; the 1934-35 and 1936 dates differ by source and are both given. Current access is supported by the Encyclopedia of Alabama and the 2026 America's State Parks guide, not by an official park page; the official alapark.com Cheaha page has no Bunker Tower text. A Cheaha State Park Facebook post titled 'Bunker Tower Road is back...' appeared in search and says the tower reopened after a television-tower repair, but the page returned only its title, so nothing from it is used; a closure and reopening date should be checked before publication. Staffing is 'occasional' per the marker, whose undated text was photographed in 2021. Height 15.2 m is the marker's approximately 50 feet. No photos added. No corrections to the brief's record; events and agency match.
